transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood), Aisha Khan (Synergia), Liam O'Connell (Synergia SRE), Priya Mehta (Synergia ML), Oliver Rossi (Synergia Security), Nora Tan (Product)

Summary (auto): 58m scoping call to align on POC success criteria, workload characterization (QPS, concurrency, token distributions), benchmark plan and timeline. Customer wants a pilot/benchmark that demonstrates cost/latency tradeoffs for conversational payments flows and PCI-adjacent tokenization endpoints.

Topics: POC goals, traffic etiology, QPS baselines, concurrent session behavior, input/output token length distributions, tail latency targets, security/compliance gating, pilot timeline and next steps.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um we'll run about an hour. quick intros?
[00:10] Aisha Khan: hi all, i'm aisha, i run platform at synergia. we own the infra for payment routing and the new conversational payments assistant.
[00:18] Liam O'Connell: liam, sre, i'll be running the benchmark env and looking at tails.
[00:23] Priya Mehta: priya, ml eng. i'll share the traffic samples after this call.
[00:27] Maya Chen: great. ravi and diego from our side will go deep on perf. the goal today is to pin success criteria and a reproducible benchmark for a 2-week pilot.
[00:36] Ravi Patel: yeah hi, quick heads up, we'll want both steady-state QPS and burst scenarios, and also the token distribution cause that drives memory and kv cache behavior.
[00:46] Nora Tan: clarifying question, what do you mean by kv cache? we've heard it called a few things.
[00:50] Diego Alvarez: it's our in-memory key-value cache for prefix caching — sometimes auto-called KV cache — sorry if terms differ. it helps with repeated conversation turns.
[00:58] Oliver Rossi: quick security note, we need to confirm KMS integrations and whether the private deployment supports our HSM — that's a gating item.
[01:05] Maya Chen: noted, we'll include KMS/HSM support docs. okay, let's go through current traffic. priya, can you summarize?
[01:13] Priya Mehta: sure. average QPS is 4.5 during business hours, peaks up to 120 for marketing pushes, but that's for short bursts, like 90s. median session length ~3 turns, mean tokens per input 45, output tokens 65 — but some auth flows generate 400+ tokens when we include logging/context.
[01:34] Ravi Patel: ok that variance is really important — a few 400-token responses changes GPU memory and batching. do you have percentiles for request sizes?
[01:42] Priya Mehta: yeah p50 input 38, p90 120, p99 380. outputs similar skewed. session concurrency: we see about 2.2 concurrent outstanding requests per active user on average, but system-wide concurrent in-flight requests can be 260 during peak.
[02:00] Liam O'Connell: and note that concurrency spikes are correlated with batch end-of-day reports around 02:00 UTC for a subset of merchants — it's a synchronized push.
[02:09] Maya Chen: perfect. so for the POC we'll need: steady state at 5 QPS, controlled bursts to 120 QPS for 2 minutes, and a tail test hitting p99 token sizes. does that sound right?
[02:20] Aisha Khan: yes, also add a mid-range sustained 30 qps for 10 minutes test to simulate promo traffic.
[02:26] Ravi Patel: agreed. we'll design a 6-scenario benchmark: idle, steady 5 qps, sustained 30 qps, short 120 qps bursts, p99 token stress, and a mixed conversation replay.
[02:37] Nora Tan: success criteria from product: sub-200ms median generation latency for short-turn flows (<= 64 output tokens), 95th percentile under 750ms, and 99th under 2s for our chat assistant. for tokenization /rule-based flows higher latency is acceptable.
[02:56] Maya Chen: i'll write that down. on the cost side, finance wants a projection: expected $/1M tokens and also a worst-case cost estimate for bursts.
[03:06] Priya Mehta: also want to validate quality: we need a tiny eval set of 200 prompts to ensure no regression vs baseline model before we change quantization.
[03:16] Diego Alvarez: noted — we'll add a quality gate tied to the benchmark run. if quality drops more than 2% on BLEU-like metric or NDCG for reranking flows, we'll pause quantized configs.
[03:27] Liam O'Connell: from infra, we need network egress ceilings and region placement. we can't have traffic cross the atlanta region for merchant data. do you support region pinning?
[03:36] Ravi Patel: yes — smart routing lets you pin to region or fall back. for private deployment we can deploy in their VPC to satisfy data residency.
[03:44] Oliver Rossi: confirm SOC 2, iso27001? and audit logs for per-request tracing.
[03:49] Maya Chen: yes, we have SOC 2 and ISO attestations and a per-request audit trail in console, we'll send the security pack.
[03:55] Priya Mehta: on the model side, which model would you recommend? our use case includes short chat and auth flows, plus a few long-document parsing for disputes.
[04:04] Ravi Patel: start with the 13B open model in our catalog — it's a good balance. for the long responses we can test a 70B variant in the pilot only for p99 validation. also we'll try int8 quantized builds for cost tests.
[04:16] Aisha Khan: will int8 affect correctness for things like PCI token redaction? we need assurance.
[04:22] Diego Alvarez: that's why we do the quality gate first, and we can selectively pin endpoints handling sensitive ops to non-quantized variants.
[04:30] Maya Chen: timeline check: propose benchmark design + template (this week), customer provides traffic sample by Jan 27, initial bench run week of Feb 8, then a 2-week pilot with Canary on day 1, full run and report by Feb 26.
[04:45] Nora Tan: that timeline works for our PM.
[04:48] Priya Mehta: quick detail — our traffic contains PII in some example utterances; we will scrub before sharing.
[04:53] Maya Chen: perfect.
[05:00] Ravi Patel: digging into measurement: we'll capture median, p95, p99 tail latency for both generation and total request time, tokens per second, GPU utilization, and memory high water mark. also we'll log failed completions and top error types.
[05:13] Liam O'Connell: for error budget, we need retries suppressed during bursts to measure system behavior — otherwise client-side retries hide true tail.
[05:20] Diego Alvarez: recommended approach: run with an 'no-retry' harness for burst tests, and a 'production-like' harness for steady-state.
[05:29] Aisha Khan: do you have a load script we can run in our staging?
[05:32] Ravi Patel: yes we'll share a JMeter/locust script plus a small nodejs harness that replays conversation sessions respecting inter-message delays.
[05:41] Maya Chen: let's talk about scaling policy expectations for Dedicated vs Hosted. synergia is interested in predictable latency at peak for business-critical flows, so dedicated capacity is attractive.
[05:54] Priya Mehta: question: what's the auto-scaling granularity? we need sub-minute scale to absorb 120 qps bursts.
[06:01] Diego Alvarez: current autoscale reacts in 60–90s for GPU pools with burst capacity faster if you pre-warm. for strict SLOs we recommend pre-warm or dedicated reserved nodes sized to the p90 workload.
[06:13] Maya Chen: that means for 120 qps 2-minute bursts, we'd either need pre-warmed burst nodes or accept some degradation in the first 60s.
[06:21] Liam O'Connell: acceptable as long as we quantify tail percentiles during that window.
[06:25] Priya Mehta: on concurrency, how do you handle KV cache invalidation across nodes? our sessions move across instances.
[06:33] Ravi Patel: KV cache is local per node to keep latency low; we do prefix checks and a small global metadata sync. for multi-node concurrency you will see a warm-up penalty for cache miss on the first post-move request.
[06:46] Nora Tan: can we measure cache hit rates during the benchmark?
[06:49] Diego Alvarez: yes — we'll export per-route cache hit metrics and correlate with latency.
[06:55] Maya Chen: let's capture these as part of the benchmark outputs: cache hit %, GPU mem high watermark, tokens/s, latency quantiles, and quality pass/fail.
[07:06] Aisha Khan: a question on pricing: do you price bursts differently or is it token-based only?
[07:12] Maya Chen: hosted is token-based plus small ondemand burst premium for very short pre-warmed capacity. Dedicated is contract + usage. we'll include price bands in the doc.
[07:23] Priya Mehta: one more: can we run a full replay of anonymized day-of-traffic to a sandbox? that'll give us the most realistic footprint.
[07:30] Ravi Patel: yes, we recommend a replay test. if you can provide a single day with timestamps and anonymized ids, we can replay at scaled QPS and produce a deterministic report.
[07:40] Oliver Rossi: security gating — before we do replay in Redwood hosted, we need a data handling attestation and proof of scrubbing. alternatively we can run replay in private deployment.
[07:50] Maya Chen: we'll accept either; if you prefer hosted we'll need the attestation.
[07:55] Nora Tan: what's your recommended success criteria summary?
[07:59] Maya Chen: i'll summarize:
- functional: all API routes return correct structured responses for eval set (quality gate)
- performance: median gen latency <200ms for short flows, p95 <750ms, p99 <2s for chat flows; sustained 30 qps without >15% increase in p95 over baseline; burst handling to 120 qps with documented tail behaviour
- stability: <1% error rate during steady-state, acceptable errors during controlled bursts documented
- cost: projection for 1M tokens and worst-case burst cost within agreed threshold

[08:28] Priya Mehta: that looks good.
[08:31] Maya Chen: ok concrete next steps recap — maya to send benchmark template, ravi to share load harness, priya to share scrubbed traffic, diego to set up initial cluster config and perf runbook. we'll target initial perf run week of Feb 8.
[08:45] Aisha Khan: can you include a sample report format?
[08:48] Maya Chen: yes — we'll send a sample PDF with charts and an annotated CSV output.
[08:52] Oliver Rossi: and security pack?
[08:54] Maya Chen: yes, security pack + SOC/ISO docs.
[08:58] Nora Tan: scheduling note — can we do a sync after the perf run to review anomalies?
[09:02] Maya Chen: absolutely, we'll schedule a 60m review within 48h of the run.
[09:06] Aisha Khan: thanks everyone.
[09:08] Liam O'Connell: thanks.
[09:10] Priya Mehta: bye.

End transcript.

References/attachments mentioned: benchmark_template.xlsx (to be shared), load_harness.tar.gz (locust/node), security_pack_link (Redwood secure share).

Notes on transcription quality: multiple technical terms occasionally mistranscribed (eg. KV cache as "KV cash" in some auto notes), speaker overlap, and occasional truncation of long utterances.
